headlines.title: Anthropic sets price range of $70 to $78 in upcoming IPO as AI lab marches toward Nasdaq
headlines.summary: Anthropic's IPO is expected to come roughly five months after Elon Musk took SpaceX public in a record offering.
headlines.article_text: Anthropic sets price range of $70 to $78 in upcoming IPO Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 to $78 per share. Should the offering take place in mid-November as expected, it will come roughly five months after SpaceX's record IPO. Anthropic has filed to trade on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol "ANT." In this article ANT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 6:35 06:35 Anthropic sets price range of $70 to $78 in upcoming IPO Squawk Box Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 to $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the five-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut. At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. The company could end up being worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from the $965 billion valuation it announced as part of a funding round in May. Anthropic said it has entered into an agreement with Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Google , Micron , Microsoft , Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to purchase $26 billion of the company's Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the IPO price. The shares sold in the private placement will not be registered in the offering and will not be subject to lock-up agreements with the underwriters, the company said. As Anthropic executives get set to pitch the offering to investors, they have to contend with a tumultuous political environment , following last week's midterm elections that included a Democratic sweep in Congress and the passage of numerous statewide ballot measures that could slow the AI buildout. They're also facing a public market that's grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade on concern that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for companies that need it for costly infrastructure purchases. CNBC reported last week that some Anthropic investors were bracing for a lower valuation than had previously been expected. While Anthropic had been looking toward a $2 trillion valuation until recently, shareholders told CNBC that even $1.5 trillion is now in doubt, with one investor calling that number a "stretch." Should Anthropic reach the Nasdaq this month as planned, under ticker symbol "ANT," the debut would come roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion. Elon Musk's reusable rocket and AI company has a market cap of just under $2 trillion, around its valuation at the time of the IPO. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the AI lab in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, and the company primarily sells its products and services to other businesses. On Monday, Anthropic introduced two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, the first time the company has released so-called "frontier" models since Amodei called to slow down the pace of AI development in September . Anthropic said the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said. Anthropic said in its amended filing on Tuesday that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month. "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort. We hope you will share our ambition to see it though." Skydance — Sarah Min 23 Min Ago Rocket Lab shares fall as EBITDA outlook and Neutron uncertainty overshadow record revenue Shares of Rocket Lab were fell nearly 6% after the aerospace manufacturer reported adjusted EBITDA loss of $18 million for the third quarter. Rocket Lab- YTD Rocket Lab has pushed Neutron's inaugural flight into 2027 following manufacturing and testing challenges involving the vehicle's first-stage composite structures. The company reported quarterly revenue of $268 million, a 73% increase year-on-year and a record backlog of approximately $3.6 billion, a 52% increase since end of Q2 2026. Positive GAAP operating cash flow for the company was $7.2 million. Approximately $1 billion in new launch contracts have been signed across Electron, HASTE, and Neutron, bringing Rocket Lab's total launch backlog to 117 launches: a new record. The company said it secured more than $515 million of Neutron launch contracts during the quarter, increasing the rocket's backlog to 16 missions before its debut. — Deena Zaidi 27 Min Ago TSMC shares rise as October revenue jumps nearly 60% Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co . were up marginally after the world's largest contract chipmaker reported strong October sales. Its third-quarter operating margin reached 58.7%, exceeding the upper end of its guidance range. — Deena Zaidi 50 Min Ago Riot Platforms gains after Jefferies upgrade Shares of Riot Platforms were up nearly 2% after a Jefferies upgraded to buy from hold. RIOT- YTD Jefferies highlighted Riot's Corsicana-powered land lease, which it estimates will generate an average yield of roughly 33%. Jefferies estimates capital expenditure of approximately $6 million per megawatt of IT capacity, compared with $11 million to $15 million for a typical data-center build. Corsicana alone could be worth approximately $16 per Riot share, according to analysts. — Deena Zaidi 56 Min Ago Sanmina surges after guidance tops estimates Sanmina soared 19% after the electronic manufacturing services provider rolled out an outlook that came in ahead of the Street's expectations. The company's revenue forecast of $17.5 billion to $19.5 billion also came in ahead of the $16.61 billion consensus estimate. TTWO 5-day chart — Fred Imbert 56 Min Ago Hims & Hers Health slips on disappointing guidance Shares of Hims & Hers Health fell 2% after the company issued weaker-than-expected guidance for the fourth quarter. Adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges between $70 million and $90 million, also below an estimate of $105.8 million. Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.
